children: SpaceX
heads into third-quarter earnings with investors bracing for a potentially sharp move in the stock as Wall Street weighs accelerating revenue growth against enormous capital spending.
The company is scheduled to report Q3 results on
Oct. 20
Analysts expect SpaceX to post
$0.14 per share in earnings on roughly $12.9 billion in revenue
, while the options market is pricing in a
7.8% move in either direction
following the report.
Based on SpaceX's Oct. 16 closing price of $146.03, that implies a potential post-earnings trading range of roughly
That expected swing would still be smaller than the reaction following SpaceX's second-quarter report, when shares fell
13.61% in a single session
The pressure point remains spending.
SpaceX reported a
$541 million net loss in Q2
while spending $18.4 billion on capital expenditures, including $15.8 billion tied to AI computing systems.
Investors will now be looking for evidence that those investments are translating into stronger revenue and earnings.
Wall Street expectations are already rising.
Evercore analyst Kutgun Maral recently increased his SpaceX price target to
, while maintaining a Buy rating. He expects Q3 revenue to exceed consensus and projects the company could reach a
$104 billion annual revenue run rate by year-end
Pivotal Research's Jeffrey Wlodarczak also raised his target to
, forecasting Q3 revenue of $13.2 billion and EPS of $0.21.
Investor Takeaway
I think this earnings report is really a test of whether SpaceX can turn extraordinary infrastructure spending into equally extraordinary revenue growth.
The market is already pricing in a sizable post-earnings move, while analysts are pushing targets higher on expectations for stronger Starlink monetization and AI-related capacity.
That creates a high bar.
If revenue comes in above roughly $13 billion and management shows better progress toward profitability, the bull case around SpaceX's scale could strengthen materially.
But another quarter of heavy spending without enough operating leverage could revive concerns about how much capital the company will need to reach its long-term ambitions.
For investors, the key things to watch are
revenue growth, earnings, capital expenditures, AI computing capacity, Starlink Mobile adoption and management's progress toward the $100 billion-plus revenue run-rate target
SpaceX has already convinced investors that it can spend at enormous scale. This quarter may show whether the revenue engine is beginning to catch up.

title: SpaceX Stock Faces Strong Signal Before Major Earnings Test
